mainTopic: The sources for eating a בכור and for a blemished בכור, how long an owner may keep a blemished בכור, and slaughtering a בכור before an expert sees its מום
overview: This עמוד has three parts. First it finishes a back-and-forth between רב יהודה in the name of רב and the scholars of דבי רב about which words of the פסוק teach that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night, and which teach that a בכור בעל מום goes to the כהן. Each side keeps its own reading of the פסוק. Next the גמרא asks how to read the משנה's twelve months and thirty days for a בכור that got a מום. A ברייתא shows that a first-year מום near the end of the year gets extra time after the year, but only enough to complete thirty days from the מום. One version of רבי אלעזר fits this. Another version, which gives a full thirty days after the year, is refuted. Then a new משנה brings a מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר about a בכור slaughtered before an expert saw its מום. רבה בר בר חנה, backed by a ברייתא, explains that everyone forbids eye blemishes because they change after death. They argue only about body blemishes, which רבי מאיר forbids through a גזירה. The עמוד ends as רב נחמן בר יצחק begins a statement that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Why the other view does not learn from the comparison to חזה ושוק
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of דבי רב explain why they do not learn the eating time of a בכור from the פסוק that compares it to חזה ושוק. That comparison could point to the חזה ושוק of a תודה, which is eaten for only one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side: why don't they learn it from there? Because if we learned from there, one could say the בכור is like the breast and thigh of a תודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the other side (דבי רב) rejects רב יהודה's proof from the פסוק comparing a בכור to חזה ושוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two kinds of offerings have a חזה ושוק: a שלמים, which is eaten for two days and one night, and a תודה, which is eaten for only one day and one night. Since the פסוק does not say which one it means, the comparison is unclear. It could lead to the shorter time of a תודה, so it cannot prove the two-day rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one: how does the other side respond?
If it were learned from there
One could say
Breast and thigh: the parts of certain offerings given to the כהן
Thanksgiving offering, eaten for only one day and one night

steps.confusionAlert: Every וְאִידַּךְ here switches sides. The speaker alternates between דבי רב and רב יהודה, so track carefully who is answering whom.

phrases.english: And the other side: if it were learned from there,
phrases.notes: The other side here is דבי רב, who do not use this פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר חָזֶה וָשׁוֹק שֶׁל תּוֹדָה.
phrases.english: one could say it means the breast and thigh of a thanks offering.
phrases.notes: A תודה is eaten for only one day, so the comparison would give the wrong time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues earlier, where רב יהודה in the name of רב brought the comparison to חזה ושוק as his source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the חזה ושוק comparison as the source for two days and one night.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison is unclear: it could refer to a תודה, which is eaten for only one day.

steps.title: The extra word 'it shall be' adds another day
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב answers that the פסוק repeats 'יהיה לך'. This extra wording teaches an added day for the בכור, so it is compared to a שלמים and not a תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side: the פסוק says 'it shall be yours.' The Torah added another 'being' for the בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה's side defends its proof. It points out that the פסוק repeats the word 'יהיה', and says this repetition settles which offering is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק reads: 'ובשרם יהיה לך כחזה התנופה וכשוק הימין לך יהיה'. Because 'יהיה' appears a second time, it adds something extra: an extra day for eating. So the comparison must be to the חזה ושוק of a שלמים (two days), not of a תודה (one day).

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says
It shall be yours
Another use of the word 'being' (יהיה), which adds something

phrases.english: And the other side: the verse says:
phrases.notes: Now it is רב יהודה in the name of רב answering.

phrases.english: "It shall be yours"
phrases.notes: The end of במדבר י״ח:י״ח, where 'יהיה' appears a second time.

phrases.english: the verse added for you
another 'being' regarding the firstborn.
phrases.notes: This extra wording teaches an extra day of eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in Step 1 that the comparison might be to a תודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to an extra word in the פסוק that removes the doubt.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בכור might be compared to the חזה ושוק of a תודה, which is eaten for one day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra 'יהיה' adds a day, so the בכור is like a שלמים and is eaten for two days and one night.

steps.title: The extra word is needed to teach that a blemished בכור goes to the כהן
steps.stepSummary: דבי רב reply that the extra 'יהיה לך' is not free for teaching an added day. It is needed to teach that even a בכור בעל מום is given to the כהן, a rule found nowhere else in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side: you can say that this 'it shall be yours' teaches about a blemished בכור, that it is given to a כהן, since we found this nowhere else in the whole Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: דבי רב push back. They say the extra word is already being used for a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word can only be used for one new teaching. דבי רב say 'יהיה לך' teaches that a בכור with a blemish still belongs to the כהן. This law has no other source in the Torah, so the word is needed for it. That leaves nothing to teach the extra day.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal with a blemish, which cannot be brought as an offering
That one gives it to the כהן
Since we have not found it anywhere else

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source, according to דבי רב, for the הלכה that a blemished בכור is still given to the כהן, who may eat it as ordinary meat.

phrases.english: And the other side: regarding that source,
one could say:
this "it shall be yours"
teaches about a blemished firstborn
that one gives it to a priest,
since we have not found it
phrases.notes: We have not found this law stated anywhere else.

phrases.english: in the entire Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 2's use of the extra word by giving it a different job.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the extra 'יהיה' to teach an added day.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The extra word is already needed to teach that a בכור בעל מום is given to the כהן.

steps.title: רב יהודה learns the blemished בכור from 'their flesh'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב learns the law of the blemished בכור from a different word: 'ובשרם' (their flesh). Because it is plural, it includes both a תם and a בעל מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side: the פסוק says 'and their flesh', meaning both an unblemished one and a blemished one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה's side shows that it has another source for the blemished בכור. This frees 'יהיה לך' to teach the extra day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural form 'their flesh' points to more than one kind of בכור: the perfect one (תם) and the blemished one (בעל מום). So the rule that a blemished בכור goes to the כהן is already covered. That leaves the extra 'יהיה' free to teach two days and one night.

keyTerms.meaning: And their flesh (plural)
An unblemished animal

phrases.english: And the other side: it says "and their flesh"
phrases.notes: Back to רב יהודה in the name of רב.

phrases.english: both an unblemished one and a blemished one.
phrases.notes: The plural word is read as including two kinds of בכור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 3 by giving a separate source for the blemished בכור.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives an alternative source, so the disputed word is free for its original teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יהיה לך' is needed for the blemished בכור, so it cannot teach the extra day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blemished בכור is learned from 'ובשרם', so 'יהיה לך' remains free to teach the extra day.

steps.title: 'Their flesh' is plural only because it refers to everyone's firstborns
steps.stepSummary: דבי רב answer that 'ובשרם' is plural only because it speaks about the firstborns of all of ישראל. It does not include a בעל מום, so their position stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side: 'and their flesh' is said about the firstborns of all of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: דבי רב reject רב יהודה's reading of 'their flesh'. This closes the exchange, with each side keeping its own reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural does not have to mean two kinds of בכור. It is plural simply because many Jews own firstborn animals. So 'ובשרם' teaches nothing about a blemished בכור, and דבי רב still need 'יהיה לך' for that law.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn animals (plural)
Of all of ישראל
It is saying, it refers to

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute comes down to how to read the פסוק. רב יהודה in the name of רב: 'ובשרם' includes the blemished בכור, and 'יהיה לך' adds a day, so a בכור is eaten for two days and one night like a שלמים. דבי רב: 'ובשרם' is plural only because it means all of ישראל's firstborns, and 'יהיה לך' is needed for the blemished בכור, so the חזה ושוק comparison cannot prove the two-day rule.

phrases.english: And the other side:
"and their flesh" is about those firstborns
of all the Israelites, it is saying.
phrases.notes: The plural refers to many owners, not to two kinds of animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ — ״וּבְשָׂרָם״ דְּהָנֵי בְּכוֹרוֹת דְּכוּלְּהוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 4's reading of 'ובשרם', ending the exchange.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that 'ובשרם' includes a בכור בעל מום.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The plural form is explained by many owners (all of ישראל), not by two kinds of animal.

steps.title: The משנה's rule about a blemish in the first year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if a בכור got a מום within its first year, the owner may keep it for the whole twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a blemish appeared within its first year, the owner is allowed to keep it for the full twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. It is setting up a question about what this line means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a בכור should be given to the כהן quickly. The משנה gives the owner extra time: if the מום came during the first year, he may keep the animal until that year is over. The next step will ask exactly how far this extra time goes.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish that disqualifies an animal from being brought on the מזבח
Within its (first) year
He is allowed to keep it (with him)
Twelve months

phrases.english: If a blemish developed in it within its first year,

phrases.aramaic: רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: he is permitted to keep it for the entire twelve months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a new line of the משנה, separate from the earlier discussion about how long a בכור may be eaten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור that got a מום within its first year may be kept by its owner until the end of twelve months.

steps.title: How should the twelve months and thirty days be read
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה gives twelve months plus thirty more days, or whether it describes two separate cases, a first-year מום and a later מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: What is the משנה saying? Option one: if the blemish came within its year, he may keep it for the full twelve months, and after the year he gets thirty more days. Option two: if the blemish came within its year, he may keep it for the twelve months and no more; and if the blemish came after its year, he may keep it for only thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a real question about how to understand the משנה. The question is not an attack on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions both twelve months and thirty days. Option one adds them together, so a first-year מום gets the rest of the year and then thirty more days. Option two treats them as two different cases, so a first-year מום gets only until the year ends, and the thirty days belong only to a מום that came after the year.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (the חכמים)
How is it saying? (How should we read it?)
Or perhaps
And no more

steps.confusionAlert: Both options agree that a מום after the first year gets only thirty days. The only open question is whether a first-year מום also gets thirty days after the year ends.

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
How is the mishna speaking?
If it developed a blemish within its year,

phrases.aramaic: רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: he is permitted to keep it the entire twelve months,
and after its year also another thirty days?
Or perhaps:

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּנוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ,
phrases.english: where the blemish developed within its year,

phrases.aramaic: רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ
phrases.english: he is permitted to keep it the entire twelve months
and nothing more,
and where it developed a blemish after its year,
he is permitted to keep it only thirty days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to read the line of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a first-year מום get thirty extra days after the year ends, or are the twelve months and the thirty days two separate cases?

steps.title: Trying to answer from a ברייתא about a firstborn today
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. It speaks about a first-year מום and then grants thirty days after the year because of השבת אבידה. This seems to show that a first-year מום does get thirty extra days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: A בכור in our time, before it has a blemish that can be shown to a חכם, may be kept two or three years. Once it has a blemish that can be shown to a חכם, if the blemish came within its year, he may keep it the full twelve months. After its year, he may not keep it even one day or even one hour. But because of returning a lost item to the owners, the חכמים said he may keep it thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from a ברייתא. The ברייתא first discusses a first-year מום, then says that after the year the owner gets thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seems to be describing one case the whole way through: a first-year מום that lasts until the year ends. If so, the thirty days after the year apply to that same animal. That would support option one, twelve months plus thirty days. The thirty days are given as השבת אבידה, meaning time for the owner to find a כהן and hand the animal over properly.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (an introduction to a proof)
In our time, when there is no בית המקדש
To show it to a חכם (an expert who judges whether the מום counts)
Returning a lost item

steps.confusionAlert: Here השבת אבידה is used loosely. It means giving the owner time to find a כהן, not returning an animal that was actually lost.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a baraita:
A firstborn in the present time,
until it is fit to be shown to an expert,
he is permitted to keep it two or three years;
and once it is fit to be shown to an expert,
if the blemish developed within its year,

phrases.aramaic: רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: he is permitted to keep it the entire twelve months.
After its year he is not permitted to keep it

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ יוֹם אֶחָד, וַאֲפִילּוּ שָׁעָה אַחַת.
phrases.english: even one day, and even one hour.
But because of returning a lost item to the owners,
they said: he is permitted to keep it thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of step 7 from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Option one: a first-year מום allows keeping the animal twelve months plus thirty more days.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that moves from a first-year מום to 'after its year,' and grants thirty days there because of השבת אבידה.

steps.title: The ברייתא has the same ambiguity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא's thirty days 'after its year' could refer to a מום that first appeared after the year, or to a מום from before the year, so this proof fails. The next step brings a clearer ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still the question stands for me: are the thirty days for a blemish that came after its year, or perhaps for one that came before its year?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own proof. The ברייתא can be read in two ways, just like the משנה, so it does not settle anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on assuming that 'after its year' in the ברייתא continues the first-year case. It could instead be starting a new case: a מום that first appeared after the year. In that reading, it matches option two. Because both readings work, this ברייתא cannot settle the question from step 7. The next step brings a clearer source that does.

keyTerms.meaning: And still the question stands for me
After its (first) year
Before (the end of) its year

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה and the ברייתא both mention twelve months and thirty days. This ברייתא cannot decide whether a first-year מום gets extra days after the year. The next step brings a clearer ברייתא that answers this.

phrases.english: But still the dilemma remains for me:
are the thirty days for a blemish after its year,
or perhaps for one before its year?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 8 by showing the ברייתא is unclear in the same way as the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא. Both options for reading the משנה remain possible.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that 'after its year' continues the first-year case. It may instead introduce a new case of a מום that first appeared after the year.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the extra days only complete thirty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a מום that appeared fifteen days before the year ended gets fifteen days after the year. So the extra time only completes thirty days counted from the מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If a מום appeared on the fifteenth day before the end of its year, we complete fifteen days for it after its year. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to settle the question from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מום came fifteen days before the year ended, the owner still gets fifteen more days after the year. That rules out option two from step 7, which said a first-year מום gets the twelve months 'and no more' (וְתוּ לָא). Fifteen plus fifteen is thirty, so the time after the year is measured as thirty days counted from the מום.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: an opening that brings a source as a proof
We complete, meaning we fill in only the missing days
Its year, the בכור's first twelve months
Learn from this, a conclusion drawn from the source

steps.confusionAlert: Fifteen days before the end of the year does not mean the fifteenth day of the year. It means fifteen days are left in the year, so the owner gets fifteen more after it to reach thirty in total.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹלַד לוֹ מוּם בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ,
phrases.english: If a blemish developed in it fifteen days before the end of its year,
phrases.notes: Fifteen days remain in the year.

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁלִימִין לוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם אַחַר שְׁנָתוֹ.
phrases.english: we complete for it fifteen days after its year.
Learn from this,
phrases.notes: So a first-year מום does get time after the year, up to thirty days from the מום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected in step 9, a clearer ברייתא is brought to answer the same question.
steps.raayaObject: A first-year מום does get extra time after the year, counted as thirty days from the מום. This rejects option two's 'ותו לא'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a מום that appeared fifteen days before the year's end

steps.title: This supports רבי אלעזר's thirty days from the מום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the ברייתא supports רבי אלעזר, who says the owner gets thirty days counted from when the מום appeared.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי אלעזר, for רבי אלעזר said: We give him thirty days from the time the מום appeared.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא it just brought agrees with a statement of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר counts the thirty days from the moment the מום appears, not from the end of the year. The ברייתא's fifteen plus fifteen fits that counting exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Supports, meaning the source backs up someone's view
We give him extra time
From the time the blemish appeared

steps.whatToRemember: In this version, a בכור that got a מום near the end of its year may be kept until thirty days have passed since the מום appeared.

phrases.english: this supports Rabbi Elazar,
for Rabbi Elazar said:
We give him thirty days
from the time the blemish developed in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the conclusion of step 10 to an existing statement of an אמורא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's rule of thirty days from the מום

steps.title: Another version: רבי אלעזר gives a full thirty days after the year
steps.stepSummary: Some report רבי אלעזר differently. He learns from the פסוק 'שנה בשנה' that a first-year מום gets thirty full days after the year, because thirty days count as a 'year'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבי אלעזר said: From where do we know that a בכור that got a מום within its year gets thirty days after its year? As it says: 'Before ה׳ your God you shall eat it year by year.' Which days count as a year? You must say: thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of what רבי אלעזר said. In this version he holds the opposite of what the ברייתא showed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שנה בשנה' suggests eating the בכור in one year and also into the next. Thirty days are treated in some areas of הלכה as a meaningful piece of a year. So this version of רבי אלעזר gives thirty extra days after the full year, no matter when during the first year the מום appeared.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say, introducing a second version of a statement
From where do we know, asking for a source
Year by year, the words of the פסוק that are expounded
Considered a year

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion argued by someone else. It is the same רבי אלעזר, reported in a different way. The two versions disagree about what he actually said.

phrases.english: Some say: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִבְכוֹר שֶׁנּוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ
phrases.english: From where do we know regarding a firstborn that developed a blemish within its year

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנּוֹתְנִין לוֹ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם אַחַר שְׁנָתוֹ?
phrases.english: that we give him thirty days after its year?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹאכְלֶנּוּ שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה״,
phrases.english: As it is stated: 'Before the Lord your God you shall eat it year by year,'
which are the days that are considered a year?
phrases.notes: The text is corrected from אֵיזוֹ to אֵילּוּ.

phrases.english: You must say: these are thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of רבי אלעזר's statement, in which he does not agree with the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור that got a מום within its first year may be kept a full thirty days after the year, learned from 'שנה בשנה'.

steps.title: The ברייתא only completes the days and does not add thirty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second version from the same ברייתא. The ברייתא only completes the missing days. It does not give a full thirty days after the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If a מום appeared fifteen days before the end of its year, we complete fifteen days for it after its year. Completing, yes. Giving a full thirty, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second version of רבי אלעזר using the ברייתא from step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אלעזר were right, the owner should get thirty days after the year. The ברייתא gives only fifteen, just enough to complete thirty from the מום. So the ברייתא allows completing the days but not a full grant of thirty.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged, raising an objection from a תנאי source
Completing the missing days
Giving a full amount of days

phrases.english: They challenged:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹלַד לוֹ מוּם בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ —
phrases.english: If a blemish developed in it fifteen days before the end of its year,

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁלִימִין לוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם אַחַר שְׁנָתוֹ.
phrases.english: we complete for it fifteen days after its year.
Completing, yes. Giving a full thirty, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the version of רבי אלעזר given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim of a full thirty days after the year
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives only enough days to complete thirty from the מום, which shows there is no full thirty-day grant after the year.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר is refuted in this version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that this version of רבי אלעזר is firmly refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רבי אלעזר, a conclusive refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the topic by declaring that the second version of רבי אלעזר does not stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered, so the ברייתא wins. The final הלכה is the one from step 10. The owner only gets enough time to complete thirty days from when the מום appeared.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation from a source that cannot be answered

steps.whatToRemember: Final rule: a first-year מום near the end of the year gets extra time only to complete thirty days from the מום, not a full thirty after the year.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of Rabbi Elazar, a conclusive refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 13 without any answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The version of רבי אלעזר giving thirty days after the year is rejected. The days only complete thirty from the מום.

steps.title: New משנה: slaughtering a בכור before showing its מום
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. Someone slaughtered a בכור and only afterward showed its מום to an expert. רבי יהודה permits it. רבי מאיר forbids it because it was not slaughtered on an expert's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who slaughters a בכור and then shows its מום: רבי יהודה permits. רבי מאיר says: Since it was slaughtered not on the ruling of an expert, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new משנה with a מחלוקת about the order of things: slaughtering first, then checking the מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an expert must confirm the מום before the בכור is slaughtered. רבי יהודה holds that if the expert later confirms a real מום, the meat is permitted. רבי מאיר holds that skipping the expert's approval beforehand makes it forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the opening of a new משנה
One who slaughters
Shows its blemish to an expert
An expert qualified to rule on blemishes
Since, giving a reason

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who slaughters the firstborn
and then shows its blemish:
Rabbi Yehuda permits it.
Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְנִשְׁחַט שֶׁלֹּא עַל פִּי מוּמְחֶה —
phrases.english: Since it was slaughtered not on the ruling of an expert,
it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה permits a בכור whose מום was shown only after slaughter. רבי מאיר forbids it because there was no expert ruling beforehand.

steps.title: A non-expert's ruling: the בכור is buried and he pays
steps.stepSummary: If someone who is not an expert examined a בכור and it was slaughtered on his word, the animal must be buried, and he pays from his own money.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who is not an expert examined the בכור, and it was slaughtered on his word: it must be buried, and he must pay from his own house.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second case, where an unqualified person gave the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-expert's ruling counts for nothing, so the בכור was slaughtered without a valid permission and its meat may not be eaten. Because he caused the loss, he must pay out of his own pocket, to the כהן who would have received the בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who is not an expert
On his word, based on his ruling
Must be buried, so no benefit may be taken from it
Must pay from his own money

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how seriously הלכה treats ruling on a בכור without proper qualification: the meat is lost, and the person who ruled is held responsible.

phrases.english: One who is not an expert
and he examined the firstborn,
and it was slaughtered on his word:
that animal must be buried,
and he must pay from his own house.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּמְחֶה וְרוֹאֶה אֶת הַבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second case of the same משנה, about a ruling given by a non-expert.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור slaughtered on a non-expert's ruling is buried, and the non-expert pays.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה explains where the dispute really is
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה says everyone forbids eye blemishes because they change after death. ר' מאיר and ר' יהודה argue only about body blemishes: ר' מאיר makes a גזירה because of eye blemishes, and ר' יהודה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבה בר בר חנה said: With blemishes on the eye, everyone agrees the animal is forbidden, because those blemishes change. They argue only about blemishes on the body. ר' מאיר holds that we make a decree against body blemishes because of eye blemishes. ר' יהודה holds that we do not make that decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה. רבה בר בר חנה narrows down exactly what ר' מאיר and ר' יהודה are arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the animal dies, an eye blemish can look different, so an expert can no longer tell whether it was a permanent מום. Because of that, both sides forbid it. Body blemishes stay the same, so the only question is whether ר' מאיר's protective decree reaches them too.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Blemishes or film on the eye (cornea)
Blemishes on the animal's body
They change (in appearance after death)
We make a protective decree (גזירה)
Because of; out of concern for

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think ר' יהודה permits every case. Even ר' יהודה forbids eye blemishes. He permits only body blemishes.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה:
phrases.english: Gemara: Rabba bar bar Chana said:
With blemishes on the eye,
everyone agrees that it is forbidden,
because they change.
They argued only about blemishes on the body,
for Rabbi Meir holds:
we decree against blemishes on the body
because of blemishes on the eye,
and Rabbi Yehuda holds:
we do not decree against blemishes on the body
because of blemishes on the eye.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: בְּדוּקִּין שֶׁבָּעַיִן דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה dispute from Step 15 by limiting it to body blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone forbids eye blemishes because they change. The dispute is only about body blemishes: ר' מאיר makes a גזירה because of eye blemishes, and ר' יהודה does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that ר' מאיר's prohibition on body blemishes is a rabbinic safeguard, not a claim that the expert cannot judge the blemish.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבה בר בר חנה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same split. ר' יהודה forbids eye blemishes because they change and permits body blemishes because they do not. ר' מאיר forbids both.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught like this in a ברייתא: Someone slaughters a בכור and then shows its blemishes to an expert. ר' יהודה says: with eye blemishes it is forbidden, because they change. With body blemishes it is permitted, because they do not change. ר' מאיר says: both are forbidden, because they change.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up what רבה בר בר חנה just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly states that ר' יהודה forbids eye blemishes and argues only about body blemishes. That matches רבה בר בר חנה exactly. Its reason for ר' מאיר, 'because they change,' will be questioned in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a supporting ברייתא)
Shows its blemishes (to an expert)
Both this one and that one

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:

phrases.aramaic: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַבְּכוֹר וּמַרְאֶה אֶת מוּמָיו —
phrases.english: One who slaughters a firstborn and then shows its blemishes:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
with blemishes on the eye it is forbidden,
because they change;
with blemishes on the body it is permitted,
because they do not change.
Rabbi Meir says:
both this and that are forbidden,
because they change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 17 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבה בר בר חנה's claim that everyone forbids eye blemishes and the dispute is only about body blemishes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which ר' יהודה forbids eye blemishes and permits body blemishes, while ר' מאיר forbids both.

steps.title: Do body blemishes really change?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's reason for ר' מאיר. Body blemishes do not change after death, so 'because they change' cannot be the reason they are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think 'because they change'? Do body blemishes change?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the wording of the ברייתא it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says ר' מאיר forbids both kinds 'because they change.' Everyone admits that body blemishes stay the same after death. So that reason cannot work for body blemishes, and the wording needs to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (a sign that an idea does not make sense)
Do...? (introduces a question that expects 'no')

phrases.english: Can it enter your mind: 'because they change'?
Do blemishes on the body change?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the stated reason for ר' מאיר's view in the ברייתא from Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's phrase 'because they change' as ר' מאיר's reason for forbidding body blemishes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Body blemishes do not change after death. So the reason 'they change' cannot apply to them.

steps.title: Correcting the wording: because of the ones that change
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. It means body blemishes are forbidden because of the eye blemishes, which do change. This matches the גזירה in Step 17.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it as: because of the ones that change.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by slightly changing how the ברייתא is read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Because they change' becomes 'because of the ones that change.' Body blemishes do not change themselves. They are forbidden only as a safeguard because of eye blemishes, which do change. This is exactly the גזירה that רבה בר בר חנה described.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a corrected reading)
Because of the ones that change

steps.whatToRemember: According to ר' מאיר, eye blemishes are forbidden after the slaughter because they change. Body blemishes are forbidden only through a גזירה because of eye blemishes. ר' יהודה forbids only eye blemishes.

phrases.english: Rather: because of those that change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in Step 19 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that body blemishes themselves change.
steps.terutzMaskana: Body blemishes are forbidden because of eye blemishes, which change. This is a גזירה, matching רבה בר בר חנה.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק is introduced as the speaker of a new statement. The statement itself continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is only a setup. It names רב נחמן בר יצחק as the next speaker, and his actual words come in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the attribution appears on this עמוד. The content of his statement comes on the next עמוד, so there is no ruling to explain yet.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who is about to speak

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
phrases.notes: His statement continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a new speaker after the ברייתא's wording has been settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The content of the statement appears on the next עמוד.
